segments.he: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי אֵירוּסִין וְכוּ׳. פְּשִׁיטָא! לָא צְרִיכָא, דַּאֲפִילּוּ צוּרְבָּא מֵרַבָּנַן דְּנִיחָא לֵיהּ לַחֲמוּהּ לְקָרוֹבֵיהּ.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: A scribe may «not write documents of betrothal» and documents of marriage except with the consent of both the groom and the bride, and it is the groom who provides the scribe’s wages. The Gemara asks: Isn’t it «obvious» that the groom pays the wages? After all, he is the one acquiring his betrothed. The Gemara answers: «No,» it is «necessary» for the mishna to state this, to teach us «that» it applies «even» when the groom is «a Torah scholar,» in «which» case «it gives his father-in-law satisfaction to bring him into his family» by having him marry his daughter. Even in such a case, where the bride’s family is a beneficiary, it is the groom who pays the wages.
